distractors: Permission granted for one specific case only, with the next one having to come back and ask again from the start.
A decision taken without consulting anybody who might have objected, on the view that asking would have cost more time than it was worth.

Provisional agreement pending a formal sign-off, enough to start work against but not enough to spend against. What it hands you is the nod, with the actual permission still sitting somewhere ahead of you.

A budget set aside for needs nobody has foreseen, drawn on when something turns up that the plan never contained. It is money held in reserve rather than permission held in advance, and each draw still has to be released case by case.

A time-limited exemption from a rule, granted because the rule would otherwise block something urgent, and expiring on a date written into the grant itself. The exception is narrow and the clock is the whole point of it, which is nearly the opposite of a freedom whose value lies in how wide it runs.
